There is some new metaprogramming that can help here: the `to_fun` attribute.
To get access, you need to add `import Mathlib.Tactic.ToFun` to the imports (doesn't need `public`).

```suggestion
@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (-f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).neg

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma add (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f + g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).add (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
theorem sum (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (G σ)) :
    Meromorphic (∑ n ∈ s, G n) := fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.sum (h · x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma sub (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f - g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).sub (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f * g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).mul (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
theorem prod (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (F σ)) :
    Meromorphic (∏ n ∈ s, F n) := fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.prod (h · x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma div {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f / g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).div (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).pow n

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℤ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).zpow n

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma iterated_deriv [CompleteSpace E] {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) :
    Meromorphic (_root_.deriv^[n] f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).iterated_deriv
```

entries_text.P201: A dual, additive twin, projection or characterisation lemma that a generator (`to_dual`, `to_additive`, `simps`, `mk_iff`) can produce is generated, not written by hand; the declaration is placed after the lemmas the generator needs.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.deriv` is not `protected`, unlike its siblings `MeromorphicAt.deriv` and `MeromorphicOn.deriv` (both `protected theorem deriv`). Inside `namespace Meromorphic`, and anywhere `Meromorphic` is opened, the bare identifier `deriv` now resolves to this lemma instead of `_root_.deriv`. That is why the following lemmas have to write `_root_.deriv`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Declare it as `@[fun_prop] protected lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv`, then drop the `_root_.` prefixes from `fun_deriv`, `iterated_deriv` and `fun_iterated_deriv` (write `deriv f x` and `deriv^[n] f`).

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.pow` and `Meromorphic.fun_pow` take the exponent as an implicit `{n : ℕ}` before `hf`. The sibling lemmas `MeromorphicAt.pow (hf) (n : ℕ)`, `MeromorphicAt.fun_pow` and `MeromorphicOn.pow (n : ℕ)` take it explicitly after the hypothesis, as do `Continuous.pow` and `Differentiable.pow`. So `hf.pow` here and `hf.pow n` for `MeromorphicAt` are called differently.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Make the exponent explicit and put it after the hypothesis: `lemma pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (n : ℕ) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).pow n`, and `lemma fun_pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (n : ℕ) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x ^ n) := hf.pow n`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.zpow` and `Meromorphic.fun_zpow` take `{n : ℤ}` implicitly before `hf`, while `MeromorphicAt.zpow (hf) (n : ℤ)` and `MeromorphicOn.zpow (n : ℤ)` take it explicitly after the hypothesis.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Change the signatures to `lemma zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (n : ℤ) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).zpow n` and `lemma fun_zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (n : ℤ) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x ^ n) := hf.zpow n`.

findings_as_matched.claim: The new predicate has no way back to the pointwise and set notions. There is no `Meromorphic.meromorphicAt` (tagged `@[fun_prop]`) and no `Meromorphic.meromorphicOn`, the analogues of `Differentiable.differentiableAt` and `Differentiable.differentiableOn`. So `fun_prop` cannot use a `Meromorphic f` hypothesis to prove a `MeromorphicAt` goal, and users must unfold the definition by hand.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Add, inside `namespace Meromorphic`: `@[fun_prop] lemma meromorphicAt (hf : Meromorphic f) (x : 𝕜) : MeromorphicAt f x := hf x` and `lemma meromorphicOn (hf : Meromorphic f) (U : Set 𝕜) : MeromorphicOn f U := fun x _ ↦ hf x`.

findings_as_matched.claim: The `@[fun_prop]` API for `Meromorphic` has no identity or constant rule, unlike `MeromorphicAt.id` and `MeromorphicAt.const`. As a result `fun_prop` cannot prove that even `fun x ↦ x` or a constant function is meromorphic, so it fails on any polynomial or rational expression in `x`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Add `@[fun_prop] protected lemma id : Meromorphic (id : 𝕜 → 𝕜) := fun x ↦ .id x` and `@[fun_prop] lemma const (e : E) : Meromorphic (fun _ : 𝕜 ↦ e) := fun x ↦ .const e x` to `namespace Meromorphic`.

findings_as_matched.claim: The arithmetic API covers `div` but not `inv`, and has no `smul`, although `MeromorphicAt` and `MeromorphicOn` both provide `smul`/`fun_smul` and `inv`/`fun_inv`. So `fun_prop` cannot handle `(f x)⁻¹` or `f x • g x` for `Meromorphic`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Add `@[fun_prop] lemma smul {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {g : 𝕜 → E} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) : Meromorphic (f • g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).smul (hg x)`, `fun_smul` (`Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x • g x) := hf.smul hg`), `@[fun_prop] lemma inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic f⁻¹ := fun x ↦ (hf x).inv` and `fun_inv` (`Meromorphic (fun x ↦ (f x)⁻¹) := hf.inv`).

findings_as_matched.claim: `fun_sum` is proved by `simpa [← Finset.sum_apply] using (sum h)`, a simp detour with redundant parentheses. The sibling `MeromorphicOn.fun_sum` (and `sum` just above) builds the term pointwise from the existing `MeromorphicAt.fun_sum`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Replace the proof with the term `fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.fun_sum (h · x)`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `fun_prod` is proved by `simpa [← Finset.prod_apply] using (prod h)` rather than directly from `MeromorphicAt.fun_prod`, as `MeromorphicOn.fun_prod` and `prod` just above are.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Replace the proof with the term `fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.fun_prod (h · x)`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `meromorphicOn_univ` calls `tauto` to prove an iff that is just the two definitions unfolded, `(∀ x ∈ univ, MeromorphicAt f x) ↔ ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x`. That is a heavy tactic for a one-line term.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Replace `by tauto` with the term `⟨fun h x ↦ h x trivial, fun h x _ ↦ h x⟩` (on its own line after `:=`).

findings_as_matched.claim: The docstring refers to `Set.univ` without code backticks, and the statement has a double space before `:=` (`↔ Meromorphic f  := by tauto`).
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Write the docstring as `/-- A function is meromorphic iff it is meromorphic on `Set.univ`. -/` and use a single space before `:=`.

findings_as_matched.requested_change: Write `Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x)`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic` is registered as a `fun_prop` predicate, but the PR adds no transition lemma from `Meromorphic f` to `MeromorphicAt f x` (or to `MeromorphicOn f U`). As a result `fun_prop` cannot use a hypothesis `hf : Meromorphic f` to close any `MeromorphicAt` goal, and there is no dot-notation projection `hf.meromorphicAt` / `hf.meromorphicOn`. The analogous whole-space predicate `Differentiable` has `@[fun_prop] Differentiable.differentiableAt` and `@[fun_prop] Differentiable.differentiableOn`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Add to `namespace Meromorphic`: `@[fun_prop] lemma meromorphicAt (hf : Meromorphic f) {x : 𝕜} : MeromorphicAt f x := hf x` and `lemma meromorphicOn (hf : Meromorphic f) {U : Set 𝕜} : MeromorphicOn f U := fun x _ ↦ hf x`.

findings_as_matched.claim: The `fun_prop` API for `Meromorphic` lacks the identity and constant rules (and `inv`/`smul`), so `fun_prop` fails on elementary goals such as `Meromorphic (fun x : 𝕜 ↦ x)`, `Meromorphic (fun _ ↦ e)`, `Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x + e)` and anything involving `⁻¹`. `MeromorphicAt` and `MeromorphicOn` both provide `id`, `const`, `inv`/`fun_inv` and `smul`/`fun_smul`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Add in `namespace Meromorphic`: `@[fun_prop] lemma id : Meromorphic (id : 𝕜 → 𝕜) := fun x ↦ .id x`, `@[fun_prop] lemma const (e : E) : Meromorphic (fun _ : 𝕜 ↦ e) := fun x ↦ .const e x`, `@[fun_prop] lemma inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic f⁻¹ := fun x ↦ (hf x).inv`, `fun_inv`, and `@[fun_prop] lemma smul {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) : Meromorphic (f • g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).smul (hg x)` with `fun_smul`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.deriv` is declared unprotected, unlike its siblings `protected theorem MeromorphicAt.deriv` and `protected theorem MeromorphicOn.deriv`. Inside `namespace Meromorphic` a bare `deriv` then resolves to `Meromorphic.deriv`, which is why the following lemmas have to write `_root_.deriv`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Declare it as `protected lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv`, and drop the `_root_.` prefixes from `fun_deriv`, `iterated_deriv` and `fun_iterated_deriv`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.pow` (and `zpow`, `fun_pow`, `fun_zpow`) take the exponent as an implicit `{n : ℕ}`/`{n : ℤ}`, whereas `MeromorphicAt.pow hf n`, `MeromorphicOn.pow n` (and `zpow`) take it explicitly. Because `Meromorphic f` unfolds to a pi-type, the sibling-style call `hf.pow 3` still elaborates, but it means evaluation at the point `3`: it has type `MeromorphicAt (f ^ ?n) 3`, not `Meromorphic (f ^ 3)`.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Make the exponent explicit and after `hf`, as in the siblings: `lemma pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (n : ℕ) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).pow n`, `fun_pow ... (n : ℕ) ... := hf.pow n`, and likewise `zpow`/`fun_zpow` with `(n : ℤ)`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.fun_sum` is proved by `simpa [← Finset.sum_apply] using (sum h)`, a simp call (with redundant parentheses) where the pointwise lemma `MeromorphicAt.fun_sum` already gives a one-line term proof in the same style as every other lemma in this namespace.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Replace the proof with `fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.fun_sum (h · x)`.

findings_as_matched.claim: `Meromorphic.fun_prod` is proved by `simpa [← Finset.prod_apply] using (prod h)`, a simp call where the existing pointwise lemma `MeromorphicAt.fun_prod` gives a direct term proof matching the rest of the namespace.
findings_as_matched.requested_change: Replace the proof with `fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.fun_prod (h · x)`.
